newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EU membership has slowed Austrian inflation-WIFO.
newsitem.headline: EU membership has slowed Austrian inflation-WIFO.

text.p: European Union membership has knocked half a percentage point off Austrian inflation, Vienna based economic research institute WIFO said on Tuesday.
"If we had not joined the EU, the rate of inflation would have been a half percentage point higher in the first half of 1995," WIFO said in its monthly report said.
Austria joined the EU on January 1, 1995.
In August annual inflation slowed to 1.8 percent from 2.1 the previous year. WIFO has forecast annual inflation will ease to 1.7 percent this year from 2.2 percent in 1995.
"Given private consumer spending in Austria is nearly 1.3 trillion schillings, Austrian EU entry has meant a saving for consumers of around 7.5 billion schillings," WIFO said.
The first year of Austrian EU membership brought the biggest price reductions to foodstuffs, which were 2.2 percent cheaper by the end of 1995. -- Elizabeth Fullerton, Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
